requirement: Encode nested Python values into JSON-ready data by dispatching on type with functools.singledispatch, preserving Decimal digits, formatting dates in ISO form, refusing naive datetimes, non-finite floats, non-string keys and unregistered types.
skeleton: A singledispatch encode base that raises TypeError, stacked registrations for plain scalars, handlers for float, Decimal, date and datetime, a list and tuple handler and a dict handler that recurse through encode.
caption: Type-based dispatch with functools.singledispatch to turn Python values into JSON-ready data, using the standard-library math, decimal and datetime modules. encode(value) is the generic function; its base implementation raises TypeError naming the unregistered type, so a set is refused. One stacked registration passes None, bool, int and str through unchanged. The float handler raises ValueError for a non-finite float found with math.isfinite and otherwise returns the value. The Decimal handler returns str of the value so digits such as 1.10 survive. The date handler returns isoformat, and a separate datetime handler, chosen over the date handler because singledispatch follows the method resolution order and datetime subclasses date, raises ValueError for a naive datetime without tzinfo and otherwise returns isoformat. Lists and tuples, registered together, become lists of encoded items. Dicts become new dicts whose values are encoded recursively, raising TypeError naming the key type when a key is not a string. The fixture asserts that plain values pass through, that Decimal 1.10 encodes as 1.10, that a date and a UTC datetime encode in ISO format, that a naive datetime and both nan and inf raise ValueError, that a nested dict holding a tuple, a Decimal and a date encodes recursively and survives a json round trip, that an int key raises TypeError, and that a set raises TypeError.

plan.intent: Serialize application data safely to JSON
constraints: Unregistered types and non-string dict keys raise TypeError
Naive datetimes and non-finite floats raise ValueError
Decimal values keep their exact digits as strings

rationale.teaches: singledispatch registration by explicit type, stacking registrations, and dispatch resolving the most specific class in the MRO.
rationale.why: An isinstance chain or a missing subclass handler silently routes datetime through the date branch, and forgetting to recurse leaves unencodable values buried inside containers.

ops.docstring: Encode Python values into JSON-ready data with functools.singledispatch.

candidates.why_wrong: Without a datetime handler dispatch falls back to the date handler, so naive datetimes are accepted.
Only list is registered, so a tuple reaches the base implementation and raises TypeError.
Dict values are copied without encoding, so nested Decimal and date values stay unencodable.
Converting Decimal to float drops trailing digits and can lose precision.
nan and inf are returned unchanged and produce invalid JSON when serialized.
